paragraphs: Geniva, in Rav’s time, when he would go to his house. Rav visited Geniva’s house, and Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba was praying behind Rav: Berakhot 27a. In the name of Rabbi—a scribal error; it should read “in the name of Rav.” Rav Yosef said, “May his Master forgive Geniva”: Berakhot 25a. In the name of Rav: Avodah Zarah 36b. Ravina said: Geniva said in the name of Rav, Chullin 44a; there, 50b: Rabbi Avina said: Geniva said …. At the end of chapter Hanizzakin he stated laws in Rav’s name and gave the sages a doubled greeting, as to a king. Geniva said in the name of Rav Assi: Chullin 50b. Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said, “It was explained to me in the name of Nanniva” [as printed], there. He disputed with Mar Ukva and pressed him. Mar Ukva sent to Rabbi Elazar that it was in his power to hand him over to the government. He wrote to him, “Be still before the Lord, and He will cast them down, slain upon slain.” Immediately Geniva was put in a neck-chain: Gittin chapter 1, 7a. In chapter Hitkabbel—a scribal error; it should read Haomer—in Gittin 65b, Geniva went out in a neck-chain to be executed by the government and gave 400 zuz to Rabbi Avina (see his entry). In chapter Hanizzakin, 62, end of side a, Rav Huna and Rav Yehudah—it should read Rav Chisda, as it also does in newer Talmud editions—were sitting, and Geniva was walking by. One said to the other, “Let us stand before him, for he is learned.” He replied, “Shall we stand before a contentious man?” Rashi explains: one who disputed the sages’ words, for he used to trouble Mar Ukva, who was head of the court. At the end of chapter Kol HaGet, 31b, Rav Huna and Rav Chisda were sitting and Geniva passed, and he said, “Thus said Rabbi Chanan bar Rava.” In Midrash Kohelet, on “As he came forth from his mother’s womb,” Geniva said concerning a fox that found a fenced vineyard …. Adda B.B.Ch.; Geniva in the name of Rav.
